author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Nearly 300 people in New Hampshire may lose full Medicaid coverage on October 1 as new federal eligibility limits take effect, according to state figures reported by NHPR.

The Department of Health and Human Services identified 296 residents who could be affected. Under the change, adults who are not pregnant generally must be a U.S. citizen or national, a lawful permanent resident, a Cuban-Haitian Entrant or a migrant covered by the Compacts of Free Association to keep full Medicaid eligibility.

Eligibility rules are not changing for people younger than 19, pregnant patients or women during the year after pregnancy. Some residents who lose full benefits may still qualify for emergency Medicaid, and others may be able to seek coverage through the insurance marketplace.

The change is especially consequential for people receiving ongoing or long-term care. State officials said they contacted everyone identified as potentially affected, though one family profiled by NHPR disputed receiving notice. Residents who believe their status is incorrect can contact the state or a benefits counselor before coverage changes.
dek: State health officials identified 296 people whose full coverage may end when federal eligibility rules narrow for some noncitizens.
headline: Nearly 300 New Hampshire residents may lose Medicaid October 1
